Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. ## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about Saba. None is used in this draft.
- Wording a scholar should check first: 34:16 (the Arim, and the plants), 34:19 (tales, scattered completely), 34:15 (the dual form of the gardens), 34:19 (make the distances longer), 34:21 (that We might know).
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Marib, the dam of Marib, the scattering of the tribes of the south and the dates; none is used.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. A land of favour  (`#a-land-of-favour`)

Cited ayat: 34:15, 34:18

> **34:15** لَقَدْ كَانَ لِسَبَإٍ فِى مَسْكَنِهِمْ ءَايَةٌ جَنَّتَانِ عَن يَمِينٍ وَشِمَالٍ كُلُوا۟ مِن رِّزْقِ رَبِّكُمْ وَٱشْكُرُوا۟ لَهُۥ بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ وَرَبٌّ غَفُورٌ

> **34:18** وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ ٱلْقُرَى ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا قُرًى ظَٰهِرَةً وَقَدَّرْنَا فِيهَا ٱلسَّيْرَ سِيرُوا۟ فِيهَا لَيَالِىَ وَأَيَّامًا ءَامِنِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (34:15): The Quran says that there was a sign for Saba in their dwelling place: gardens on the right and on the left.

**c2** (34:15): They were told to eat of the provision of their Lord and to give thanks to Him, for theirs was a good land and a forgiving Lord.

**c3** (34:18): God placed between them and the towns He had blessed visible towns, and measured the journey between them.

**c4** (34:18): They were told to travel in them by night and by day in safety.

### One-minute summary

The Quran says that Saba had a sign in their dwelling place, gardens on the right and on the left [c1]. They were told to eat of the provision of their Lord and give thanks to Him [c2], and to travel in safety between visible towns [c3][c4].

### Complete story

The Quran says that there was a sign for Saba in their dwelling place: gardens on the right and on the left [c1]. They were told to eat of the provision of their Lord and to give thanks to Him, for theirs was a good land and a forgiving Lord [c2]. God placed between them and the towns He had blessed visible towns, and measured the journey between them [c3]. They were told to travel in them by night and by day in safety [c4].

### Deep study

- The Quran says that there was a sign for Saba in their dwelling place: gardens on the right and on the left (34:15) [c1].
- They were told to eat of the provision of their Lord and to give thanks to Him, for theirs was a good land and a forgiving Lord (34:15) [c2].
- God placed between them and the towns He had blessed visible towns, and measured the journey between them (34:18) [c3].
- They were told to travel in them by night and by day in safety (34:18) [c4].

### Kids mode

The people of Saba had gardens on the right and on the left [c1]. They were told to eat what their Lord provided and to thank Him [c2]. They could travel safely from town to town [c3][c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The first ayat give the favours before the account of what the people did with them [c1][c2][c3]. One reading is that gratitude is the response the passage asks for [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: where Saba was, when it flourished, who ruled it or how many people lived there; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: the Arabic of 34:15 uses a dual form for the gardens; the draft says gardens on the right and on the left.
- Not established: which towns are the towns He had blessed, and where the visible towns stood; the ayat do not say.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Yemen, Marib and the dam later accounts connect with Saba; none is used here.

## 2. Turning away and scattering  (`#turning-away-and-scattering`)

Cited ayat: 34:16-17, 34:19-21

> **34:16** فَأَعْرَضُوا۟ فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَيْلَ ٱلْعَرِمِ وَبَدَّلْنَٰهُم بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَوَاتَىْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ وَأَثْلٍ وَشَىْءٍ مِّن سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ
>
> **34:17** ذَٰلِكَ جَزَيْنَٰهُم بِمَا كَفَرُوا۟ وَهَلْ نُجَٰزِىٓ إِلَّا ٱلْكَفُورَ

> **34:19** فَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَا بَٰعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنَا وَظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَحَادِيثَ وَمَزَّقْنَٰهُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَٰتٍ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ
>
> **34:20** وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُۥ فَٱتَّبَعُوهُ إِلَّا فَرِيقًا مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
>
> **34:21** وَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ عَلَيْهِم مِّن سُلْطَٰنٍ إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ مِمَّنْ هُوَ مِنْهَا فِى شَكٍّ وَرَبُّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ حَفِيظٌ

### Claims

**c1** (34:16): They turned away, and God sent on them the flood of the Arim.

**c2** (34:16): He replaced their gardens with gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote trees.

**c3** (34:17): The Quran says that this was their recompense for their disbelief, and asks whether any is recompensed in this way but the ungrateful.

**c4** (34:19): They said, our Lord, make the distances between our journeys longer, and they wronged themselves.

**c5** (34:19): God made them tales and scattered them completely.

**c6** (34:19): The Quran says that in this are signs for every patient and grateful person.

**c7** (34:20): Iblis proved true his opinion about them, and they followed him except a group of the believers.

**c8** (34:21): Iblis had no authority over them, but it was so that God might know who believes in the Hereafter and who is in doubt about it, and your Lord is a guardian over all things.

### One-minute summary

The Quran says that the people turned away, and God sent on them the flood of the Arim and replaced their gardens [c1][c2]. It calls this their recompense for disbelief and says that God made them tales and scattered them [c3][c5].

### Complete story

They turned away, and God sent on them the flood of the Arim [c1]. He replaced their gardens with gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote trees [c2]. The Quran says that this was their recompense for their disbelief, and asks whether any is recompensed in this way but the ungrateful [c3]. They said, our Lord, make the distances between our journeys longer, and they wronged themselves [c4]. God made them tales and scattered them completely [c5]. The Quran says that in this are signs for every patient and grateful person [c6]. Iblis proved true his opinion about them, and they followed him except a group of the believers [c7]. Iblis had no authority over them, but it was so that God might know who believes in the Hereafter and who is in doubt about it, and your Lord is a guardian over all things [c8].

### Deep study

- They turned away, and God sent on them the flood of the Arim (34:16) [c1].
- He replaced their gardens with gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote trees (34:16) [c2].
- The Quran says that this was their recompense for their disbelief, and asks whether any is recompensed in this way but the ungrateful (34:17) [c3].
- They said, our Lord, make the distances between our journeys longer, and they wronged themselves (34:19) [c4].
- God made them tales and scattered them completely (34:19) [c5].
- The Quran says that in this are signs for every patient and grateful person (34:19) [c6].
- Iblis proved true his opinion about them, and they followed him except a group of the believers (34:20) [c7].
- Iblis had no authority over them, but it was so that God might know who believes in the Hereafter and who is in doubt about it, and your Lord is a guardian over all things (34:21) [c8].

### Kids mode

The people turned away from thanking God [c1]. A great flood came, and their gardens were changed [c1][c2]. The Quran says that there are signs in this for everyone who is patient and thankful [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage ends with signs for the patient and grateful, after the account of those who were ungrateful [c3][c6]. One reading is that the ayat set the loss of a land of favour beside the call to give thanks [c1][c3][c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the Arim is a word read in more than one way (a dam, a flood, a kind of rain); the draft keeps the word as the ayah gives it.
- Not established: the draft does not say when the flood came, or how many lives it cost; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: the sense of the plants named in 34:16 (the bitter fruit, tamarisk and lote) is read in more than one way.
- Not established: how Iblis proved true his opinion, or what the group of believers did; the ayat say only that they followed him except a group.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the account of the dam of Marib, the emigration of the tribes and the date; none is used here.
